ghs.en: Miki graced us with her presence.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese simply and pointedly says that Miki was there. 'Graced us with her presence' adds an ironic social judgment.

highlights.text: Miki graced us with her presence.

ghs.en: Taichi: "Come ooon, you freshman over there!"

rows.en: “Oh, look. You’re properly dressed this time.”

rows.jp: 「もうチムチムは露出してないんですね……よかったぁ」
rows.en: “And your widdle pee-pee isn't hanging out anymore... Thank goodness.”

ghs.en: Miki: "The pee-pee isn't in public anymore, is it... that's good!"

rows.en: “Do not speak of the widdle pee-pee.”

rows.jp: 「なぜ露出していたのか自分でもわからんのだ」
rows.en: “I don't even know why it was hanging out.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And why it was exposed I still don't know."

ghs.assessment: The narrator asks why Miki has fallen completely silent. The English changes the question into a statement that her silence is mysterious.

rows.jp: 「それよりこのダンボールは何かね？」
rows.en: “More importantly, what's with the cardboard box?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "More importantly, what's that cardboard box?"

rows.jp: 「あー、これでもうひと遊びしようかと思ったんですが……バレちゃしょうがないですね」
rows.en: “Oh, I thought I'd squeeze one more game out of it... but now that you've spotted me, I guess that's that.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Ahhh, I thought I'd play around with this a bit... but I've been found out, nothing I can do."

rows.en: “Are you sure you want to call it that?”

rows.jp: 「美希の家なのでミキハウス、なんの問題がありましょう」
rows.en: “It's Miki's house, so it's MIKI HOUSE. What's the problem?”

ghs.en: Miki: "It's the house of Miki therefore Miki House. Are there any problems with that?"

rows.jp: そう言われればそうか。
rows.en: When she put it that way, perhaps there was none.

ghs.en: Well, if she says so, but...

rows.jp: 「敵地で発見されぬよう行動する時などに用います」
rows.en: “It’s for moving through enemy territory without being detected.”

ghs.en: Miki: "It's used to remain undiscovered during mobilizations in hostile territory."
ghs.assessment: Miki says that the box is used when operating without discovery in hostile territory. 'Mobilizations' denotes organizing or deploying forces, not covert action.

highlights.text: Miki: "It's used to remain undiscovered during mobilizations in hostile territory."

rows.jp: 「ミキハウスを見たら普通のヤングアダルトは『いい子供服あるかい？』って具合にダンディーに中をのぞきこみたくなるに決まっている」
rows.en: “Any ordinary young adult who sees a Miki House is bound to lean in and ask, with great sophistication, ‘Got any nice children’s clothes?’”

ghs.en: Taichi: "On sight of the Miki House, a normal Young Adult will dandy up and with a, 'could there be some quality children's clothing inside?', decide to peek into it."
ghs.assessment: The English sentence is syntactically broken: a normal young adult does not 'dandy up,' and the nested question and infinitive never form a coherent clause.

highlights.text: Taichi: "On sight of the Miki House, a normal Young Adult will dandy up and with a, 'could there be some quality children's clothing inside?', decide to peek into it."

rows.jp: 「……うう、わたしの身につけているものくらいしかお売り出来ないですね」
rows.en: “...Then I'm afraid the only merchandise I can sell you is what I'm wearing.”

ghs.en: Miki: "...ngh, and it's impossible to sell something that I've already worn, isn't it."
ghs.assessment: Miki says that all she could sell would be what she is currently wearing. The English says that selling something already worn is impossible, reversing the proposition.

highlights.text: Miki: "...ngh, and it's impossible to sell something that I've already worn, isn't it."

ghs.en: Taichi: "How much should I pay for it?"

rows.jp: 「どうしてそんな突然リアルな顔をして言うんですか？」
rows.en: “Why did that suddenly get so real?”

ghs.en: Miki: "Why are you saying this making this very Real Serious face all of a sudden?"
ghs.assessment: The English duplicates 'making this' and adds inconsistent capitalization to an otherwise ordinary reference to a suddenly serious face.

highlights.text: Miki: "Why are you saying this making this very Real Serious face all of a sudden?"

rows.jp: 「リアル世代だからだ。だがそんなことはどうでもいい」
rows.en: “Because I’m from the real generation. Never mind that.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because it's a Real-Life Generation. But, that is inconsequential."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that he is of the 'real generation.' The English makes an unspecified thing into 'a Real-Life Generation' and leaves the joke grammatically incoherent.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because it's a Real-Life Generation. But, that is inconsequential."

rows.jp: 小悪魔みたいな、悪戯っぽい顔をしてみせる。
rows.en: She put on a teasing little-devil smile.

ghs.en: She makes a mischievous face that is so much like a little demonic imp's.

rows.jp: 「じゃあ一式百万円。即決価格。ただし今のみのタイムセールス。今お支払いできるなら、この場で脱いでお渡ししてもいいですよ。でもそれ以外はダメー」
rows.en: “One million yen for the complete set. Buy-it-now price. Today only, while supplies last. If you can pay me right now, I’ll take everything off and hand it over on the spot. No other terms accepted.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Well, complete set's a million yen. Buyout price. However, it's limited time sale. If you can pay now, I will strip on the spot and hand all over, no problem. Outside of this, nooot happening."

rows.jp: 桜庭からもらった金貨を十枚渡した。
rows.en: I handed her ten of the gold coins Sakuraba had given me.

ghs.en: I hand over ten of the gold coins I received from Sakuraba.

ghs.assessment: 即決 here means that the decision or deal is made immediately. 'Impulse buy' instead describes an unplanned consumer decision.

rows.jp: 空気を意味する疑問語を発して美希の表情は凍結する。
rows.en: Miki uttered a question word meaning air, and her expression froze solid.

ghs.en: Miki's expression freezes having shot off a questioning mumble that sounds like a literal translation of the Japanese word 'kuuki'.
Taichi: "...I desire you to strip on the spot."

rows.jp: 「着画がないのは残念だが、せめて脱衣シーンは撮影させてもうぞ」
rows.en: “It's a shame there were no photos of you modeling them, but at least let me film you taking them off.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Too bad there's no worn-on-model shot for demonstration, but at least the stripping scene will be photographed for sure!"

rows.jp: カメラを用意する。部室で良かった。
rows.en: I readied the camera. Good thing we were in the clubroom.

ghs.en: I set up the camera. Good thing we're in the club room.

rows.jp: バッテリーはまだ十分にあるな、よし。

ghs.en: There's still enough battery charge left, great.

rows.jp: 「十万円金貨だ。美希は知るまいが」
rows.en: “One-hundred-thousand-yen gold coins. I wouldn’t expect you to know.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ten thousand yen gold coins. You likely don't know about them, Miki."
ghs.assessment: 十万円金貨 identifies 100,000-yen gold coins. The English calls them 10,000-yen coins, an order-of-magnitude error.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ten thousand yen gold coins. You likely don't know about them, Miki."

rows.jp: 「昭和の時代は戦争したり発展したり世界に嫌われたりしながら、６０年以上も続いたのだよ」
rows.en: “The Showa era lasted more than sixty years—through war, development, and the rest of the world hating us.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The Showa Era was an era of war, an era of progress, an era of being hated by the world that lasted for more than 60 years."

rows.jp: 「そこいらじゃ使えないが、まあ正式な通貨だぞ」
rows.en: “You can't spend them just anywhere, but they're legal tender.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That they're not, but, well, they're still officially currency."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that the coins cannot be used around here but are nonetheless legal tender. The English answers only that they are not spendable and omits the local limitation.

highlights.text: Taichi: "That they're not, but, well, they're still officially currency."

rows.jp: 「さあ、即決した。入金も済んだ。次はそっちの番だ」
rows.en: “The sale is final. Payment has cleared. Your turn.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That was an impulse buy after all. So, the money due was given. Next it's your end of the bargain."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that the immediate deal is concluded and payment completed. 'That was an impulse buy' misreads 即決, and 'the money due was given' is an unnatural passive.

highlights.text: Taichi: "That was an impulse buy after all. So, the money due was given. Next it's your end of the bargain."

rows.jp: 「もし約束を違えるのであれば……『たいへん悪い』という評価をつけるぞ」
rows.en: “If you refuse to honor our agreement... I will be forced to leave you a VERY BAD rating.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Supposing you were to alter the deal... I would give you a rating of 'Very Negative'!"
ghs.assessment: 約束を違える means to break the promise. 'Alter the deal' permits modification rather than expressing breach.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Supposing you were to alter the deal... I would give you a rating of 'Very Negative'!"

rows.jp: 「女の子にとって、その噂はピンチ中のピンチです」
rows.en: “For a girl, a reputation like that is the direst emergency imaginable.”

ghs.en: Miki: "But for a girl, to have that on her shoulders is to be in a pinch among pinches!"
ghs.assessment: Miki says that such a reputation would be the worst possible crisis for a girl. 'A pinch among pinches' is a literal calque, and 'have that on her shoulders' does not identify the damaging rumor.

highlights.text: Miki: "But for a girl, to have that on her shoulders is to be in a pinch among pinches!"

ghs.assessment: なら脱ぎたまえ is a direct, pompous command to strip. 'Gladden me with stripping' invents a motive of pleasing the speaker and is not idiomatic.

ghs.en: Miki: "Ah, aWaaah, fwah... it-, it's just..."

rows.jp: 「……わたしが、かわりに脱ぎます」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I... I will strip in her place!"

rows.jp: 「えーーーーーーーーーーっ！？」
霧はスカートの中に手を入れて、下着をずりおろす。
rows.en: Kiri reached beneath her skirt and began pulling down her underwear.

ghs.en: Kiri puts her hands under the skirt, and sliiides her underwear down.

rows.jp: 「ＯＫＯＫ、いいよいいよ！　やっぱなし！」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Okieh okieh, 's enough, 's enough! I don't really want you to!"
ghs.assessment: やっぱなし means that Taichi calls the plan off after all. 'I don't really want you to' describes his desire rather than retracting the demand.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Okieh okieh, 's enough, 's enough! I don't really want you to!"

rows.jp: 「乙女を泣かせる趣味はない」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I don't have the hobby of making the ladies cry."

rows.jp: せめて二人っきりなら……。
……俺、悪者なんだね、この世界だと。
rows.en: ...So in this world, I was the villain.

ghs.en: ...I'm just the bad guy in this world, am I.
